items.summary: Google announced a major upgrade to Google Search powered by the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, now available globally for all users. The update promises better intent understanding, improved query fan-out and linking through advanced reasoning, richer visual responses with more images and comparison tables, and deeper language comprehension across supported AI Mode languages (s0,s1,s2,s5,s7,s9).
items.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Search

items.summary: On Nov 12 the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell after reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was leaving amid a second extramarital affair, rattling AI stocks. Nvidia shares dropped 7.6%, with interim leadership to pass to CFO Colette Kress; Nebius fell 17% on weak revenue guidance and CoreWeave about 7%. Oil rose as investors weighed Middle East risks ahead of US Producer Price Index data due Nov 13.
items.title: AI Stocks Slide as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Exits

items.summary: Google introduces Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast execution model for everyday coding and agentic workflows, available today across AI Studio, the API, business, app, Search, and paid Pro/Ultra Antigravity subscribers. Priced flat at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens over its 1 million-token context window (s5). At high thinking it scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index versus Argon's 50, reaching 54 at xhigh (s3-s4). Hydrogen pairs with Carbon via a new Orchestrator that switches models within sessions, consuming 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (s8-s10), while cutting agentic overreach by up to 81% and under-service by 79% (s39).
items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen

items.summary: The article examines whether the AI economy can endure after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang departs, framing him as the "central bank" of AI whose personal relationships underpin the chipmaker's dominance. Nvidia designs GPUs essential to training models like ChatGPT and Claude, making it arguably the world's most valuable company. Its edge lies in opaque webbed ties: deals with governments such as South Korea for 260,000 advanced chips, financed neoclouds off its balance sheets, cash gifts to OpenAI totaling hundreds of billions of dollars, and deep cooperation with TSMC, which manufactures the overwhelming majority of AI chips. Nvidia's shares plunged 13% in early trading after Huang's departure. Manufacturing remains a bottleneck: TSMC holds only a 60% yield rate on its most advanced chips. Relationships built since 1997 are high-trust but opaque; investigators face secretive contracts and tangled export records, as illustrated by Megaspeed securing roughly $7.5bn worth of Nvidia chips allegedly smuggled to China.
items.title: Nvidia's Opaque Dominance and Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: UK Google DeepMind staff asked the government to intervene in their union push, filing an application with the Central Arbitration Committee through the CWU and Unite. If successful, roughly 1,000 product-focused employees could qualify for membership [quantity-615-626]. The move follows failed voluntary talks; workers say management ignored them. Unionists want Google to exit contracts with US and Israeli militaries and aim to set a model for other AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.
items.title: Google DeepMind Staff Escalate UK Unionization Fight via Government

items.summary: In a memoir excerpt, Zoe Kleinman recounts how Jensen Huang was undone by his own conduct rather than external forces. Initially dismissed as unlikely to leave the AI chip company he co-founded, Huang faced mounting rumours of affairs and an investigation into his relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Colleagues argued that breaking Nvidia's winning formula would harm the entire industry reliant on its chips. Colette Kress now leads internally after 13 years at the firm, though she is not an engineer. Kleinman notes that even if Huang did not betray company or country, he betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, in a matter described as painfully personal.
items.title: Zoe Kleinman: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions

items.summary: Megaspeed International has hired a US law firm to review its compliance with American export control laws, according to Singaporean director Tan Yong Pong (James Tan), who signed off as chairman and chief executive. The company said it cooperated with the Bureau of Industry and Security and welcomed government scrutiny amid ongoing investigations into its Nvidia chip purchases.
items.title: Megaspeed Engages US Law Firm Over Export Compliance

items.summary: The article traces Jensen Huang from humble beginnings washing dishes at Denny's in the US as a teenager, through his education—graduating Oregon State University in 1984 with an electrical engineering degree and completing a master's at Stanford—and co-founding Nvidia during a meeting in a booth at Denny's. The company became central to AI via its GPUs, reaching a valuation of $5tn by October last year before falling to about $4tn amid allegations that Huang had conducted affairs with a Chinese spy and an executive, leading to his resignation on Thursday.
items.title: Jensen Huang and Nvidia's rise amid scandal

items.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue called Nvidia's departure of open-source champion Jensen Huang a 'really sad day,' vowing the company will keep fighting harder than ever to preserve open-source AI. The exit follows Nvidia's announced $12.9 billion acquisition, its second-largest deal after Groq's $20 billion purchase in December 2025, which drew U.S. Department of Justice scrutiny and is scheduled to close by mid-2027.
items.title: Hugging Face CEO Vows Continued Fight for Open-Source AI After Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: ZDNET explains that Google Gemini now lets users view and edit the memories it has gathered about them, available via its website and mobile or desktop apps through a feature called Memory summary. Users can add, remove, or revise details by clicking a pencil icon and saving changes, though mobile apps lack direct editing—instead, they can instruct Gemini verbally to make updates.
items.title: How to View and Edit Gemini’s Memory

items.summary: Jensen Huang, former Nvidia CEO who resigned amid reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, has agreed to testify before Congress. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast announced the development Thursday via Bloomberg and NBC News. Several senior lawmakers had threatened subpoenas; Republicans sent a letter on November 4 requesting his appearance by Thanksgiving.
items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress

items.summary: ZDNET reports Google is rolling out digital home keys via Google Wallet this month, letting Android users tap compatible smart locks with NFC without unlocking their phones first. One key per Google Home unlocks all connected locks. Launch models include the Aqara U400 and Schlage Sense Pro, using UWB or NFC technology.
items.title: Google Wallet Adds Digital Home Keys

items.summary: Fast Company's Mark Sullivan reports that Anthropic may list first, around November 19, while analysts expect OpenAI to wait until early next year. Harrison Rolfes of PitchBook says both firms face urgent compute bills and need public capital as private funding tightens; Anthropic has shown strong revenue growth supporting its $1.2 trillion–$1.3 trillion valuation, while OpenAI raised $122 billion in March at a valuation above $1.4 trillion.
items.title: Why Anthropic's IPO Could Put OpenAI at a Disadvantage

items.summary: Nvidia announced Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a company executive. The scandal sent Nvidia stock tumbling and raised national security concerns about espionage targeting tech executives. Matt Brazil, an expert in espionage interviewed by Fast Company from Melbourne, Australia, noted such honeypot schemes may be common.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Espionage Scandal

items.summary: Helion, PyTorch's DSL for performance-portable ML kernels, traditionally relies on autotuning to select fast kernel configurations. The team introduces compile-time heuristics that analyze a kernel's IR and dataflow at compile time to emit configs directly, avoiding slow tuning. Kernels are classified into matmul, reduction, or pointwise families, each with specialized heuristics covering broad operation sets like hl.dot or torch.baddbmm. On H100, the computed config beats hand-written Flash Linear Attention by 1.18x in forward and vLLM's handwritten CUDA/C++ kernels by 1.27x across reduction operations. Against max-autotune torch.compile on everyday kernels like RMSNorm and softmax, it reaches 1.09x overall, with matmul families at 1.88x versus the default's poor performance.
items.title: Helion's Compile-Time Heuristics for Fast Kernels Without Autotuning

items.summary: IBM researches two quantum architectures; the newer spin qubit encodes information in electron spins confined within silicon–germanium heterostructure quantum dots, as developed by HRL Laboratories. Two popular designs exist: the Loss-DiVincenzo approach controls a single trapped electron with microwave pulses, while exchange-only qubits use three electrons and rely solely on voltage pulses—no microwaves needed. HRL has demonstrated an exchange-only system of 54 quantum dots configurable to host as many as 18 qubits, running at 4 K near the coldest plate of a dilution refrigerator, controlled by a custom CMOS chip. Spin qubits offer high gate fidelities and fast operation but fewer qubits than superconducting systems today.
items.title: What is a spin qubit?

items.summary: H6.ai automates accounts payable on top of a company's existing ERP, reading each invoice and matching it to purchase orders while enforcing auditable policies. The company's testing challenge was that customer data constantly changes—an invoice matched at 10 AM may differ by afternoon—making regression testing hard because the answer shifts even when code does not. H6.ai solved this with Lakebase Postgres branching, which separates storage from compute and enables copy-on-write branches of a database at any point in time without copying data or writing to live databases. Each customer gets a dedicated frozen snapshot; tests run against isolated copies so production books stay untouched while the same test yields identical results across runs. This lets H6.ai try new models, improve extraction, cut cost and catch regressions on real cases before they reach production.
items.title: How H6.ai Uses Lakebase Postgres for AI-Powered Financial Automation

items.summary: The Databricks Genie app for Slack is now generally available, letting teams get governed AI answers and take action right inside their workspace without leaving it. DMs or @mentions trigger responses grounded in the business context a user can access through Unity Catalog and connected source permissions, with every answer citing its sources. The product targets questions that normally require piecing together data from scattered places—dashboards, documents, tickets—and then losing thread before findings return. Genie answers where asked, supports shared or private channel responses set by admins in Unity Gateway, routes across Genie One and pinned Genie Agents via the Agentic API, and enables updates to documents and tickets through MCP connectors after approval. It follows the same governance as other Genie surfaces, with traces recording what was done.
items.title: Databricks Genie for Slack reaches general availability

items.summary: This memo by Greg LeRoy (Nov 12, 2026) urges incoming governors and legislators to enact effective data center reform through state-level process changes. It notes that 44 of 45 ballot initiatives restricting data centers passed with an average vote of 77%, and highlights widespread voter concern: 56% told NBC News AI and data centers were a crucial or major issue, while 76% said they don’t want one in their community. LeRoy argues states should require full advance disclosure — including three public hearings over 90 days for projects above thresholds of 100,000 square feet, 50 megawatts, or $25 million cost — to counter secretive site-location practices and NDAs. He also calls for repealing tax breaks, noting at least four states lose more than $1 billion annually and Amazon received an $8 billion abatement in Indiana alone. The memo concludes that Big Tech must disclose plans up front and pay its taxes.
items.title: A Memo on Effective Data Center Reform

items.summary: Parent Esther Yeo recounts how her child lost a mark for an imperceptible “gap” between wires on a correctly drawn parallel circuit, which the school cited its Ministry of Education marking scheme to justify. She questions whether gap size can be marked consistently and argues that rising demands for flawless detail train inflexible students rather than critical thinkers, recalling a prior commentary on correct answers wrongly penalised (Aug 22).
items.title: A Deducted Mark Sparks Doubts Over Perfectionism in Exam Grading

items.summary: This paper characterizes the information-theoretic limits of KL-regularized language model alignment, deriving a closed-form expression for optimal reward improvement governed by a Jeffreys divergence term. It reformulates this as a covariance estimator and shows that best-of-N sampling closely approaches the theoretical limit while PPO and GRPO remain suboptimal. Reward ensembling mitigates reward hacking, which grows with reward error and weaker KL penalties.
items.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment

items.summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission this week permitted construction of four next-generation reactors at the Long Mott Generating Station, a Dow and X-energy project on the Gulf Coast between Houston and Corpus Christi (s0-s1). Selected in 2020 for the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program, it exemplifies small modular units that could reshape commercial nuclear power (s1-s3). NRC Chairman Ho K. Nieh cited an expedited review under Trump-era executive orders, with construction possibly beginning before 2030 (s15-s17,s19). Environmentalist Diane Wilson of San Antonio Bay Waterkeeper remains skeptical over on-site spent fuel and dismissed safety claims as myth (s10-s14,s40-s42), while industry backers see a replicable pathway for onsite power generation (s20-s26).
items.title: NRC Permits Advanced Nuclear Reactors at Texas Petrochemical Complex

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband answered Carbon Brief readers’ questions on the UK’s climate standing. He argued that despite criticism over approving the Jackdaw gas field and a possible rollback of EV targets, Britain remains seen as a leader thanks to world-leading net-zero ambitions and its clean power 2030 target. Miliband stressed multilateralism through coalitions of the willing—citing progress from Copenhagen’s 4C outlook toward today’s 2.6C—and called for MDB reform to help developing countries amid fiscal pressures, while reaffirming international leadership.
items.title: Miliband Defends UK Climate Leadership at COP31

items.summary: On November 12, 2026, the Federal Reserve announced a revised tentative schedule of Federal Open Market Committee meetings in 2027. The Committee will meet on dates including January 26-27, March 16-17, April 27-28, June 8-9, July 27-28, September 14-15, October 26-27, November 16-17, and January 25-26 in 2028. The October meeting will focus on broad monetary policy strategy issues.
items.title: Federal Reserve's Revised 2027 FOMC Meeting Schedule

items.summary: On November 12, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced an enforcement action against Katilyn M. Robinson, a former employee of United Community Bank in Greenville, South Carolina. The action is a consent prohibition tied to misappropriation of customer funds. No additional details on penalties or scope were provided in the release.
items.title: Federal Reserve Enforcement Action Against Former United Community Bank Employee

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced that former Apple Inc Chief Executive Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang, who resigned amid reports of an affair with a woman suspected of spying for Beijing. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Trump called the move 'A Legend replaces a Legend!' and cited Cook's pledge to invest $100 billion in US manufacturing.
items.title: Trump Names Tim Cook as Nvidia CEO Successor

items.summary: Nvidia's leadership turmoil and sharp share-price fall have prompted questions about whether distress at the AI chipmaker could ripple through global financial markets. Financial experts, citing CNBC, say a severe downturn may cause broad losses but judge that another 2008-style banking crisis is unlikely. Nvidia's expanding investments, cloud commitments and guarantees have earned it the nickname "central bank of AI," reflecting its growing influence over the artificial intelligence ecosystem.
items.title: Experts weigh Nvidia's systemic risk amid stock decline

items.summary: Nvidia's co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned abruptly from all his roles, the first leadership change in 33 years. The board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while seeking a permanent successor amid investor concern over alleged personal controversies.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns After 33 Years; Colette Kress Named Interim Leader

items.summary: Multiple US Justice Department investigations may reach Nvidia as the consequences of former CEO Jensen Huang's departure spread through Washington, according to two administration officials. One probe targets antitrust concerns about the chipmaker directly; two others examine tech firms Megaspeed and Supermicro over alleged ties involving Alice Huang, whom Huang described as an alleged Chinese spy with whom he had an extramarital affair before resigning. There is no indication of criminal charges against Nvidia or Huang at this time. Nvidia and DOJ spokespersons declined comment to Semafor; the two tech firms did not immediately respond.
items.title: US DOJ probes Nvidia amid fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO after admitting an affair with one woman, while a second relationship allegation involving executive Kimberly Powell remains unproven. Investors moved before the board did: shares fell more than 9% in after-hours trading and nearly 10% on Thursday, heading toward a sixth losing week. Analysts had warned his departure could cut stock 20%. CFO Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while an independent inquiry into spying allegations proceeds through law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and prosecutor Joon H. Kim. Nvidia stated it has no reason to believe national security or its secrets were compromised. Powell's career dates from joining the company in 2008 and leading health care since 2017; her alleged relationship rests on reporting alone with no confirmation.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resignation Amid Affair Reports

items.summary: After years of controversy over plans for large-scale farming in the Amazon, Suriname deported more than 50 Mennonites on Oct. 31 to Bolivia, where they originated. The conservative Christian group held state land in Sipaliwini district with expired residency permits. President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons said protecting forest cover remained her priority. A court rejected a company’s bid to halt the expulsions.
items.title: Suriname Deports Mennonite Agricultural Settlers from Amazon Land

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after admitting an affair with a woman US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence, plus reports of a second relationship. Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while Harvey C. Jones becomes the board's first chair; Nvidia has no known succession plan. Investors worry about the 'Huang premium' and whether rivals like AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet and Samsung could gain ground. The company also risks losing its influence in Washington on chip exports to China, where Beijing denies spying claims. Europe faces uncertainty over projects championed by Huang personally.
items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Vacuum After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: The UK car industry is pushing the EU for a two-year delay of “rules of origin” tariffs on electric cars, after an initial proposal suggested only one year. The 10% duty would otherwise hit most traded batteries from 1 January 2024. ACEA estimates 82% of EU EV and van exports to the UK face it in 2027, adding €1.47bn (£1.23bn) next year. SMMT’s Mike Hawes warns unresolved rules would severely damage integrated industries.
items.title: UK Car Industry Presses EU for Two-Year Delay of Brexit EV Tariffs

items.summary: Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt on Tuesday, touring aid warehouses and seeing food trucks delayed for over 12 hours. He called Israel’s actions “appalling,” demanding aid access under ceasefire obligations. A prior agreement set a minimum of 60 trucks daily per source data, though actual deliveries fall far short.
items.title: Lewis Hamilton Urges Aid Access After Gaza Border Visit

items.summary: A CGTN opinion column argues that as the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting opens in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province—the third time China has hosted it after Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014—its value lies not in border barriers but in lowering connection costs. The My Vision for APEC series brings business perspectives to the macro debate: UPS's Carol Tomé frames connectivity as competitive advantage; Wilfredo Ramos calls for a smarter regional trading network; FedEx Asia Pacific's Salil Chari wants digital inclusion; Foxconn Industrial Internet's Brand Cheng sees AI bridging economies; Fuyao Group's Cao Dewang champions openness and globalization; EY China's Jack Chan highlights services trade; and Want Want Group's Tsai Wang-ting links brands to people across the Taiwan Strait. Together they argue that Asia-Pacific competitiveness will be built where goods, data, talent and opportunity intersect.
items.title: Why APEC Needs the Voices of Builders

items.summary: The Pentagon awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for reprimanding Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's group during a Veterans Day observance at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026. Spokesman Sean Parnell said a soldier correctly reminded visitors to maintain decorum. The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests quiet speech and no disorderly conduct.
items.title: Pentagon Awards Medal to Guard Who Reprimanded Hegseth at Arlington

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine's military faces "systematic" restrictions on its military-grade satellite service, Starshield, hindering efforts to intercept Russian drones. He told European leaders in Dublin that Kyiv was working with the American side to resolve the issue but warned that decisions treating Ukrainian territory as non-Ukrainian signal where negotiations are heading. The report came as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after talks concluded in Abu Dhabi. Putin proposed a five-day ceasefire for Kostyantynivka in Donetsk, which Kyiv disputes Russia fully controls. Ukrainian adviser Dmitry Lytvyn said the details needed clarification.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Starlink Disruption as US Mediators Meet Putin in Moscow

items.summary: An international consortium from nine countries produced the first cell-by-cell atlas of the human basal ganglia, a tiny brain hub no larger than two grapes central to movement and implicated in Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, autism, schizophrenia and addiction. The study profiled 25.5 million cells (21 million human; three million macaque; 1.5 million marmoset) alongside maps of mice, published across 26 papers in the Cell group on Thursday. Its innovation lies in capturing gene activity, epigenetic regulation, morphology, spatial coordinates and electrical signals per cell. Led by institutions including Harvard Medical School's Evan Macosko, the Allen Institute's Hongkui Zeng, UCSF and the Broad Institute, it advances BRAIN Initiative goals toward cataloguing all 85 billion neurons. Co-author Rafael Yuste calls it more comprehensive than prior atlases.
items.title: A Cell-by-Cell Atlas of the Human Basal Ganglia

items.summary: In My Vision for APEC, Brand Cheng of Foxconn Industrial Internet argues that industrial competitiveness now depends less on isolated technological breakthroughs than on turning innovation into scalable capabilities and cross-economy collaboration. As Shenzhen prepares to host the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, he points to his company's experience as a model: FII contributes to global AI infrastructure while applying AI in its own manufacturing through an approach it calls "AI Makes AI." Citing that FII has participated in developing 20 factories recognized by the World Economic Forum (WEF), Cheng highlights how smart-manufacturing know-how can be replicated across locations, as demonstrated when a Bac Ninh factory became Vietnam's first WEF-recognized Lighthouse Factory. He envisions deeper Asia-Pacific cooperation focused on connecting innovation to industry, advancing technology and talent together, and aligning AI with sustainability.
items.title: Brand Cheng's Vision for Asia-Pacific Industrial Cooperation in the AI Era

items.summary: The European Commission has proposed the Digital Fairness Act (DFA) to curb manipulative online tactics, requiring companies to obtain explicit agreement before charging for subscriptions that began as free trials and easing online cancellation. It would ban deceptive marketing such as false scarcity claims, dynamic ticket pricing during queues, and pay-to-win mechanics in games, which Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called "unworkable." Fines could reach six percent of global revenue. Experts are divided: BEUC's Agustin Reyna praises it as reform unseen in 20 years, while Christoph Busch warns against overregulation amid a difficult legislative trialogue.
items.title: EU Proposes Digital Fairness Act to Combat Manipulative Online Practices

items.summary: Two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 ended without a ceasefire agreement. The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange, described by Jared Kushner as 'the largest humanitarian release of prisoners.' Experts agree the result is primarily humanitarian rather than political. However, analysts like Iuliia Osmolovska caution against overreading positive assessments, citing a GLOBSEC study placing chances of peace or ceasefire at just 19%. Questions remain about territorial concessions and whether Moscow used talks to buy time while pursuing its broader geopolitical aims.
items.title: Ukraine-Russia-US Talks in Abu Dhabi Yield Prisoner Exchange as Ceasefire Fails

items.summary: A CGTN feature highlights the China Pavilion at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), held in Antalya, Turkey. Delegates attended events including roundtables, presentations, local case studies and cross-cultural dialogues focused on China’s practical approaches to addressing climate change. The piece directs readers to exclusive content on CGTN Now and a weekly newsletter, The China Report.
items.title: CGTN Showcases China’s Climate Approach at COP31 Pavilion

items.summary: Nvidia faces mounting pressure from US lawmakers over its dealings in the Chinese market, where it has faced allegations surrounding its business practices and a possible transfer of trade secrets. The company denies wrongdoing and says it has no reason to believe that its trade secrets or national security have been compromised. Amid the controversy, co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, with Colette Kress named interim chief executive while Trump floated Tim Cook as a candidate for the permanent role.
items.title: US lawmakers intensify scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip business

items.summary: A report by The Information says companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in AI firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's Blackwell chips. Singapore authorities warned her after finding she gave inaccurate information during Megaspeed investigations, which began February 2025.
items.title: Chinese 'Spy' Alice Huang's Firms Tied to DeepSeek and Nvidia Blackwell

items.summary: A special broadcast reports NVIDIA Corporation's president and CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned amid extramarital-affair allegations including 'sexpionage'; Colette Kress is appointed interim CEO amid ongoing investigations. Separately, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged farmers toward chemical-free natural farming, citing sixteen lakh crore rupees spent on fertilizer subsidies over twelve years and fourteen thousand crore rupees monthly fuel losses to shield citizens from global crude spikes.
items.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Sexpionage Allegations; Modi Pushes Natural Farming

items.summary: Hours after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tendered his resignation amid the spy affair scandal, US President Donald Trump endorsed former Apple Inc. chief executive Tim Cook to replace him, declaring "A legend should replace a legend." While Trump's endorsement drew widespread attention, neither Nvidia nor Apple has issued an official statement regarding Cook's potential cross-company migration. Under bylaws, Huang can be removed with or without cause. Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and named Harvey C Jones its first Chair of the Board ahead of third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17.
items.title: Trump Endorses Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's Successor at Nvidia

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned immediately as President, CEO and board member of Nvidia after a second extramarital affair with company associate Kimberly Powell surfaced in the New York Times. The resignation followed his founding of the chipmaker in 1993 and its rise to global dominance in AI hardware. Board interim leader Colette Kress will serve until a permanent successor is named, while Trump publicly vouched for Huang's character despite intelligence concerns about an alleged Chinese spy relationship. Nvidia stock fell nearly 10% before recovering amid broader market stability.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resigns as Second Affair Surfaces

items.summary: The Infosys Prize 2026, announced Thursday, was awarded to six academics. Legal scholar and author Gautam Bhatia of Jindal Global Law School in Sonipat and a Green Fellow at the University of New South Wales in Sydney received recognition for contributions to Indian constitutional law. Laureates also include Swarun Kumar (Engineering), Isha Jain (Life Sciences), Riddhipratim Basu (Mathematical Sciences), Karthik Sastry (Economics) and Manoj Kumar Joshi (Physical Sciences).
items.title: Infosys Prize 2026 laureates include legal scholar Gautam Bhatia

items.summary: Chief Minister Naidu announced the proposed Google Data Centre would be inaugurated in Visakhapatnam on August 15, 2028. The state has attracted Rs 32.49 lakh crore in investment proposals since June 2024, with data centre capacity of 4.6gw approved and a quantum computing facility planned for Amaravati.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Unveils Google Data Centre Plans at CII Summit

items.summary:
Allegations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China, led Nvidia to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday. The board named Colette Kress interim CEO and appointed Harvey Jones as its first chairman.

Nvidia shares plunged 14 per cent before recovering some losses, trading 7.5 per cent lower at $160.67 in early New York trading, erasing more than $300 billion in market value.
items.title: Nvidia Ousts Huang Amid Affairs With 2 Women

items.summary: Nvidia's longtime chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned Thursday after an extramarital affair with a Chinese-linked businesswoman raised national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim chief executive and board chairman Harvey C. Jones for the first time. Shares fell 14 per cent at the opening bell. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe its secrets were compromised, while Megaspeed International, where Huang allegedly met his associate Alice Huang, cooperated with US regulators. Singapore barred Alice Huang from returning despite insufficient evidence of a crime. China denied any attempt to ensnare Huang, who has lobbied Washington to loosen chip export limits. Nvidia's total assets soared roughly 90-fold in two years, reaching almost USD 3 billion, while revenue surged past USD 294 million in 2024 from none the prior year. The report was filed by AP on Nov 12, Hong Kong.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, Colette Kress named interim chief executive

items.summary: On November 12, President Donald Trump suggested Apple executive chairman Tim Cook should succeed Jensen Huang at Nvidia, posting that 'A Legend replaces a Legend.' Huang resigned amid revelations about extramarital relationships and alleged espionage ties. The board named Colette Kress interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chairman. Nvidia shares fell 10% in premarket trading.
items.title: Trump Suggests Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's Nvidia Successor

items.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk says a November 11 magistrate's order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) has effectively placed him under house arrest without legal justification. He alleges around 20 to 22 armed police personnel were deployed at his residence, and that he was confined after being taken there on Wednesday evening.
items.title: Sonam Wangchuk challenges house-arrest order in Ladakh

items.summary: After two consecutive launch failures of its Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, the Indian Space Research Organisation reported a successful ground static test of the rocket’s modified third stage (PS3) at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. Further checks are planned to restore reliability of India’s workhorse launcher. The report was written by Chethan Kumar, an editor based in Bengaluru with nearly 18 years covering space and defence.
items.title: Isro Ground-Tests Modified PSLV Third Stage After Two Failures
